messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC next steps and workload intake

Thanks again for your time today, Alex — great conversation and excited to get the POC moving. Below is a concise recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned heading into the technical intake. Please confirm or correct anything I missed.

Summary / success criteria
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference for AcmeHealth triage assistant: latency < 250ms p95 for interactive flows, average cost per 1K tokens under target (we can finalize once we see traffic), and end-to-end output quality meeting your accuracy/recall thresholds on the provided eval set.
- Success criteria: p95 latency <= 250ms for 0.5–2s response flows; error rate < 1%; manual QA pass rate >= 90% on the 200-case evaluation set.

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): intake + environment setup; exchange workload profile and access.
- Week 1: deploy trial endpoints (dedicated staging capacity), run smoke tests.
- Week 2: run evaluation workload against the trial endpoints; collect latency/cost/quality metrics.
- Week 3: iterate on tuning (batching, quantization profile), finalize evaluation report and next-step recommendation.

Owners / contacts
- Redwood PM/AE: Ben Carter (me) — overall coordination, commercial items.
- Redwood SE: Marissa Cole — technical intake and config, will lead the tech call.
- CSM: Dylan Brooks — success criteria tracking and post-trial handoff.
- AcmeHealth: Alex Reed — POC sponsor and primary contact.

Workload & traffic intake (please confirm values below or paste your traffic_profile.csv):
- Typical interactive RPS (avg): 8 requests/sec
- Peak RPS (sustained spikes): 60 requests/sec (short bursts up to 90 for 30–60s)
- Concurrency (simultaneous open requests): 6
- Avg prompt length (tokens): 120 tokens
- Avg response length (tokens): 80 tokens
- Max total tokens per request (prompt + response): 512 tokens
- 95th percentile token length: 400 tokens
- Burst patterns: heavy morning ingest/reporting window 02:00–03:00 UTC (batch runs lasting up to 10 minutes, concurrency bump to ~40), intermittent interactive spikes tied to patient triage events lasting 30–60 seconds.
- Auth: API key initially, will evaluate VPC/private later for Prod.
- SLO tolerance: we should target p95 latency 250ms for typical interactive flows, allow higher for batch windows.

Next steps (action items)
- Alex: share representative sample traffic_profile.csv + the 200-case eval set by EOD Friday.
- Marissa: will schedule a 60-minute technical intake (proposal: Mon 24 May 09:00 PT).
- Ben: I’ll send an evaluation plan & kickoff doc (attached) and a calendar invite for the intake call.

Attachments: AcmeHealth-POC-eval-plan.xlsx, traffic_profile_template.csv

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@acmehealth.com>

Subject: Re: POC next steps and workload intake

Ben — this looks great, thanks for the clear plan. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- The avg RPS you listed (8) sounds right for interactive triage, but our peak numbers are occasionally higher when multiple intake streams fire concurrently. We saw sustained peaks ~75 rps in our load test last quarter; short-lived spikes reached ~110 rps for <45s.
- Token lengths: average is ~100–130 tokens prompt, and responses average ~100 tokens; some of our incident summaries push total tokens near 700 (rare, but they exist).
- Batch job detail: the heavy batch runs you saw are actually nightly backfills that run in parallel across 6 worker pods — that drives concurrency and short peaks. They typically start at 02:15 UTC and finish within 12–18 minutes.

I’ll attach a sanitized sample traffic_profile.csv and the 200-case eval set by EOD Friday. Can Marissa confirm whether Redwood needs service account access during the trial or if we can stick to API keys + test dataset?

Thanks,
Alex Reed
Senior Product Manager, AcmeHealth
alex.reed@acmehealth.com
+1 (617) 555-0110

Alex — thanks for the detail, that helps. Updated intake notes based on your reply and a few Redwood recommendations below.

Confirmed / updated workload profile (please confirm these numbers after you upload the CSV):
- Typical interactive RPS (avg): 8 rps
- Peak sustained RPS: 75 rps (short spikes up to ~110 rps for <60s)
- Concurrency: 6 for interactive, up to 40 during nightly backfills.
- Avg prompt tokens: 110 tokens; avg response tokens: 100 tokens; allow for rare requests up to 700 tokens total.

Redwood recommendations for trial config
- We’ll provision a small dedicated staging pool with autoscale headroom to handle 110 rps bursts and concurrency up to 50 for the nightly window. This keeps interactive p95 latency tight while absorbing backfill spikes.
- Suggest running the 200-case eval at low-traffic hours to prioritize latency measurements; we’ll also run a synthetic replay to estimate cost.
- If you can provide a short list of 10 canonical prompts that represent the worst-case token lengths, that will help us tune batching and KV cache behavior.

Ownership / next steps
- Marissa: please schedule the tech intake with Acme devs (proposed Mon 24 May 09:00 PT) and confirm whether API keys are sufficient or if you need service account access.
- Dylan: I’ll loop you into success criteria tracking and the evaluation dashboard setup.
- Alex: please upload the traffic CSV + eval set and share any compliance constraints for trial data handling.

I’ll attach an updated POC schedule and a small checklist for the tech intake.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
